brief: tiktok for my gym, something that hooks

context.audience: people who keep promising to start in January

concept: Day 1 vs Day 90, told only through the sound and speed of one person's breath on the same treadmill.
plan_outline: 1. CU · eye · static · gym at night, fluorescent light · a man in his twenties, red-faced, gasping on a treadmill (2 s, the hook: a face in distress)
2. ECU · eye · static · same treadmill · the treadmill's speed dial turned up; the screen a soft glow, no readable numbers (1.5 s)
3. CU · eye · static · same treadmill, same framing · the same man, leaner, breathing steady, a slight smile (2 s, the match cut)
4. MS · low · track · gym floor · he walks off the treadmill toward camera, towel over his shoulder (3 s)
5. End card (page) · '90 days. Start Monday.' + logo (2 s)
why: A jump cut on identical framing is the transformation; social viewers read it instantly.
Sound design (gasping → steady breath) carries the story for viewers with sound on; the faces carry it muted.
Numbers on the machine would come out garbled, so the screen stays a glow and the numbers go on the card.
